dovish.title: Labour Market Softening
dovish.summary: Job market is cracking: payrolls went negative, far below forecast.
dovish.reason: Payrolls turned negative and prior months were revised lower, signalling a labour-demand inflection and strengthening the insurance-cut case. Friday's NFP benchmark revision (forecast -620k) is a downside risk to the dovish narrative if confirmed larger.

dovish.title: ISM Manufacturing Back in Contraction
dovish.summary: Factories are shrinking again — demand is cooling, not overheating.
dovish.reason: Sub-50 output, new orders and employment point to weaker demand and hiring, while lower prices paid reduces the inflation obstacle to easing. Aug 28 Chicago PMI (forecast 57.0) is a near-term test.

dovish.title: Consumer and Industrial Chain Under Pressure
dovish.summary: Consumer engine sputtering: biggest US retailer cut guidance.
dovish.reason: Softer retail guidance and industrial orders can transmit through earnings, hiring and consumption, reinforcing the slowdown narrative. Aug 28 UoM Consumer Sentiment (forecast 51.0, prev 51.0) will test the sentiment leg.

dovish.title: Long-End Easing Continues — Passive Tightening Fading
dovish.summary: 10Y -1.4% w and 30Y -1.6% w; term-premium/passive-tightening counter-narrative softening.
dovish.reason: Long-end has eased -1.4% w (10Y 4.672% from 4.738%) and -1.6% w (30Y 5.191% from 5.276%); softened the term-premium/passive-tightening hawkish counter-narrative. Intraday +0.2bp bounce is noise vs the multi-day trend. Still rich vs forecast 4.80% but the trend is now dovish.

dovish.title: Equity Rally Confirms Risk-On Into Jackson Hole
dovish.summary: SPY +0.7% w, QQQ +1.1% w; calmest VIX in two months — dovish-friendly tape.
dovish.reason: Thu 2026-08-27: SPY +0.66%, QQQ +1.37%, IWM +0.29% on the day; weekly SPY +0.70%, QQQ +1.08%, IWM flat. VIX -4.60% d to 14.51 — multi-week low. Risk-on posture heading into Jackson Hole (opens 20:00 ET tonight) consistent with dovish pricing. Sector mix Thu: XLE -0.22% d, XLI -0.85% d, XLF -0.65% d — defensives and bonds outperforming, growth leading. Drivers stay dovish-tilted.

dovish.title: Oil Demand-Scare — Cumulative Hit Intact
dovish.summary: WTI -2.1% w despite intraday recovery; demand scare not yet reversed.
dovish.reason: WTI recovered to $83.19 on Thu (+1.17% d) but still down 2.12% w from prior $85 level. The cumulative demand-scare signal persists: ISM 48.7 mfg, payrolls negative, China PMI weak. Intraday recovery is not a reversal — multi-day repricing intact. Driver weight held at 1.5; dovish bias unchanged.

dovish.title: VIX at Multi-Week Low — Calmest Tape Pre-Jackson Hole
dovish.summary: VIX 14.51, down 4.1% w — markets pricing benign Jackson Hole outcome.
dovish.reason: VIX dropped to 14.51 — multi-week low — heading into Jackson Hole, implying the market is pricing a balanced or dovish Fed message. Equivolume to dovish drivers; supports the dovish bias.

hawkish.title: Services PMI Big Beat
hawkish.summary: Services economy is running hot, not slowing.
hawkish.reason: Strong services demand, employment and prices paid point to persistent core-services inflation and raise the hurdle for a cut. Aug 28 Chicago PMI (forecast 57.0) and UoM 1Y inflation expectations (forecast 4.3%) are next tests.

hawkish.title: Tariff Inflation Shock
hawkish.summary: Broad reciprocal tariffs add direct imported inflation while expectations are already elevated.
hawkish.reason: Broad reciprocal tariffs add direct imported inflation while inflation expectations are already elevated. First post-tariff Core PCE release date not in current 7-day FXStreet window (likely delayed to Sep 5 post-Jackson Hole); UoM 1Y/5Y expectations on Fri 8/28 are the near-term test.

hawkish.title: Hawkish 3-Vote Dissent at July FOMC
hawkish.summary: Three regional Fed presidents wanted a hike at the last meeting — the Committee is split.
hawkish.reason: Re-verified 2026-08-27 23:21Z via federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20260729a.htm: 'maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent' with Hammack (Cleveland), Kashkari (Minneapolis), Logan (Dallas) preferring +25bp. This is the highest dissent count in 2026 and signals a meaningful cluster on the FOMC views current policy as too easy.

hawkish.title: Gold's Record Run — Inflation-Hedge Bid Persists
hawkish.summary: GC=F $4636.7 (+0.84% d, +0.84% w); real-money bid for inflation protection intact.
hawkish.reason: Gold futures GC=F at $4636.7 (+0.84% d, +0.84% w) on 2026-08-27 — record zone, off the $4648.8 intraday peak seen earlier. Spot GLD 422.60 lagging (-0.18% w) — divergence suggests futures-driven institutional bid. Signal remains: investors pay for inflation protection even while pricing cuts. Weight held at 1.0 as GLD fade tempers the signal.

hawkish.title: Inflation Expectations De-Anchoring
hawkish.summary: Inflation expectations are drifting above the 3% anchor.
hawkish.reason: Five-year expectations above 3% increase concern that inflation psychology is becoming persistent. Aug 28 UoM 1Y release (forecast 4.3% from 4.3%, 5Y 3.3% from 3.3%) is a fresh check — any uptick strengthens the hawkish case.

dovish.title: US-Canada Reciprocal Tariffs
dovish.summary: US tariffs hit Canada's export engine first and hardest.
dovish.reason: Canada's dependence on US demand means tariffs can quickly reduce export orders, industrial output and employment. Aug 28 GDP MoM (forecast 0.2%) is the proximate test.

dovish.title: Household Leverage and Mortgage Sensitivity
dovish.summary: Highly indebted households cannot absorb today's rates.
dovish.reason: High leverage and mortgage renewals make Canadian demand unusually sensitive to elevated rates.

dovish.title: Global Manufacturing Pullback
dovish.summary: Global factory slowdown leads Canadian exports lower.
dovish.reason: Global manufacturing weakness leads Canadian resource and industrial exports by one to two months. Aug 28 Chicago PMI (forecast 57.0) is the US test before Sep 1 Canadian Mfg PMI.

dovish.title: Labour Market Marginal Easing
dovish.summary: Unemployment is creeping up — labour slack is building.
dovish.reason: Higher unemployment and slower wage growth indicate more labour-market slack and less wage inflation pressure.

dovish.title: CAD Firms Slightly — Sep 2 BoC Dovish Wedge Narrows
dovish.summary: USDCAD 1.3849 — CAD firmer intraday; rate-spread trade still cap on the loonie.
dovish.reason: USDCAD closed 1.3849 on Thu (-0.19% d, +0.41% w) — modestly firmer intraday but still hovering near post-hold highs. With Sep 2 BoC only 6 days away and Fed cut-vs-hold debate live, the rate-spread trade remains the cleanest dovish signal for CAD.

dovish.title: Oil Demand-Scare — CAD Terms of Trade Eroded
dovish.summary: WTI $83.19; cumulative -2.1% w erodes CAD support and BoC's hawkish buffer.
dovish.reason: Canada's terms-of-trade benefit from oil erodes when WTI drops from $85+ to $83 (-2.1% w). The BoC's prior hawkish buffer (oil $87, XLE +0.85% w) flipped to a dovish signal: USD/CAD still near 1.38 and the rate-spread trade widened, materially increasing the cut probability into Sep 2 — only 6 days away.

hawkish.title: Retail Sales Big Beat
hawkish.summary: Consumers are still spending — no collapse in sight.
hawkish.reason: Broad retail growth suggests consumption is not collapsing and gives the BOC room to wait. Aug 28 GDP MoM is the next test — a 0.2%+ print would extend the patience case.

hawkish.title: Energy Tailwind Reversed — Marked Neutral
hawkish.summary: WTI at $83.19; energy tailwind has flipped to headwind for CAD.
hawkish.reason: WTI at $83.19 (cumulative -2.12% from prior Hawkish print at $85+), flipping the energy tailwind to a headwind for CAD. Driver kept with reduced weight (0.5) to preserve stable ID and history, marked neutral until Aug 28 GDP Fri print.

hawkish.title: CAD GDP Print Friday — Make-or-Break Before Sep 2 BoC
hawkish.summary: Friday's GDP is the hardest domestic data before the meeting; forecast 0.2% MoM (re-verified).
hawkish.reason: Friday's CAD GDP is the make-or-break test before Sep 2 BoC (only 5 days). Forecast re-verified at 0.2% MoM (FXStreet) with 3.4% annualized (vs prior -0.1% annualized revision). A 0.2%+ print extends the patience case; 0.0% or lower pulls decisively dovish. Strongest single near-term data dependency for BoC.

hawkish.title: US Stickiness Spillover — Fed Path Constrains BoC
hawkish.summary: US services 56.8 + hawkish Fed dissent + 30Y 5.19% — BOC can't lead cuts too aggressively.
hawkish.reason: A BOC cut while the Fed is split (9-3 July dissent) would widen the rate gap, weaken CAD and import US inflation. BoC has to read the Fed path carefully — and the Fed now looks more uncertain than at any point in 2026 (30Y 5.19% vs 4.90% expected, services 56.8 vs 54.0).

calendar.logic: Inflation-risk emphasis pulls hawkish; dual-mandate balance pulls dovish. Dominant near-term Fed catalyst.

Expectations stable or down would ease the de-anchoring concern; an uptick above 4.5% 1Y would raise the cut hurdle.
Above 50 confirms services resilience; a sharp miss below 50 would reinforce the ISM mfg downturn narrative.
A deeper sub-50 reading confirms export-order weakness and pulls the BOC dovish ahead of next-day rate decision.

6 days away — needs Fri GDP + Mon PMI to settle. Oil weakness + USD/CAD 1.3849 + tariff drag = dovish tilt, but a strong GDP Fri can keep the BoC on hold for one more meeting. Decision time re-verified 10:00 ET via bankofcanada.ca/press/ upcoming events widget.
A sub-50 print confirms the prior mfg contraction signal; above 52 would unwind a key dovish driver.

A tariff-driven acceleration to 3.2% or higher could force the FOMC to skip the next cut.
